title: Memory ECC Error Trending
exclusions: Calculates increases in Linux EDAC cumulative correctable (`ce_count`) and uncorrectable (`ue_count`) counters only between ordered samples from the same boot and memory scope. It does not sum cumulative samples, invent a universal '10 per week' DIMM replacement threshold, guarantee DIMM attribution, detect an unreported panic, include CPU cache/PCI/AER/MCE records unless separately normalized, or diagnose memory, CPU, board, firmware, thermal, or power root cause. First samples, boot changes, counter decreases, missing EDAC drivers, missing DIMM labels, and stale polls are coverage/state findings. The hourly poll, completed-day window, severity, retention, and routing are local policy. No panic setting, page retirement, reboot, isolation, or replacement is performed.
evidence: After deployment, retain host/kernel/EDAC-driver and physical DIMM inventory; source path and scope map; collector/script/input revision; representative raw sysfs samples including boot ID; expected-host/scope, counter-reset, staleness, delay, and field health; version-controlled `linux_edac_counter_increase` search, ACL, schedule, dispatches, and rows; journal/MCE/BMC/vendor diagnostic and maintenance disposition; and dated same-boot CE/UE increase, unchanged, reboot, reset, missing-driver, missing-label, duplicate, late, recovery, and routing tests. This documentation-only review read no sysfs counter, injected no ECC error, indexed no sample, and validated no production memory.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a fixed completed-day window, ingest two ordered samples for `host=server01`, `memory_scope=mc0/dimm0`, and the same `boot_id`: first `ce_count=12,ue_count=0`, then `ce_count=15,ue_count=0`. Expect one high row with `ce_increase=3,ue_increase=0`. Repeat with UE increasing 0 to 1 and expect critical. Assert scope/label, boot ID, first/last sample times, counter values, source path, sample count, and `use_case=UC-1.4.6`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for unchanged counters; a single first sample; a decrease; samples with different boot IDs; wrong index/type; blank host/scope/boot ID; nonnumeric/negative counters; duplicate samples; and events outside the window. Separate source-health results must expose a reboot boundary, counter decrease/reset, missing expected host/controller/DIMM, no EDAC driver, stale poll, missing label, and delayed/malformed sample rather than treating them as error-free memory.

dataSources: A host-local read-only scripted input polls `/sys/devices/system/edac/mc/mc*/ce_count` and `ue_count`, plus available `(dimm|rank)*/dimm_ce_count`, `dimm_ue_count`, and `dimm_label`, and emits `index=hardware sourcetype=linux:edac` with `host`, stable `memory_scope`, `dimm_label`, `source_path`, cumulative numeric `ce_count`/`ue_count`, Linux `boot_id`, kernel/driver context, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Controller totals and DIMM totals overlap and must be kept as distinct scopes, not added together. Journal/MCE and BMC records are corroboration, not interchangeable counters.
app: A deployment-owned Splunk app containing a read-only EDAC sysfs collector, scripted input, field contract, expected-host/scope and reset/source-health searches, saved search, fixtures, dashboard, exact maintenance lookup, and runbook. The Universal Forwarder can execute the input but is not Splunkbase app 617; no generic add-on creates this custom EDAC schema.
spl:
index=hardware sourcetype=linux:edac earliest=-2d@d latest=-1d@d
| eval endpoint=lower(trim(host)), scope=lower(trim(memory_scope)), boot=trim(boot_id), ce=tonumber(ce_count), ue=tonumber(ue_count)
| where len(endpoint)>0 AND len(scope)>0 AND len(boot)>0 AND isnotnull(ce) AND isnotnull(ue) AND ce>=0 AND ue>=0
| dedup _time endpoint scope boot ce ue
| sort 0 endpoint scope _time _indextime
| streamstats current=f window=1 last(ce) as previous_ce last(ue) as previous_ue last(boot) as previous_boot by endpoint scope
| eval ce_delta=if(boot=previous_boot AND ce>=previous_ce,ce-previous_ce,null()), ue_delta=if(boot=previous_boot AND ue>=previous_ue,ue-previous_ue,null())
| where ce_delta>0 OR ue_delta>0
| stats sum(ce_delta) as ce_increase sum(ue_delta) as ue_increase earliest(_time) as first_increase latest(_time) as last_increase latest(ce) as latest_ce latest(ue) as latest_ue latest(dimm_label) as dimm_label latest(source_path) as source_path latest(boot) as boot_id count as increasing_intervals by endpoint scope
| eval severity=if(ue_increase>0,"critical","high"), event_time=strftime(last_increase,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), use_case="UC-1.4.6"
| table event_time endpoint scope dimm_label severity ce_increase ue_increase latest_ce latest_ue increasing_intervals boot_id source_path use_case
| sort 0 -ue_increase -ce_increase endpoint scope
description: Calculates same-boot increases in Linux EDAC cumulative correctable and uncorrectable memory-error counters at each separately identified controller or DIMM scope. It reports observed deltas and preserves current totals without incorrectly summing cumulative samples or asserting a universal replacement rate.
value: New correctable errors can provide early evidence for hardware investigation, while an uncorrectable error is urgent even if the host remains available. Correct delta math and explicit scope help teams correlate DIMM, controller, kernel, BMC, workload, and maintenance evidence without inflating counts or replacing the wrong component.
implementation: Inventory EDAC-capable hosts and physical DIMM mappings, qualify each kernel driver's exported scopes, and collect cumulative counters plus boot ID hourly through a read-only script. Keep controller and DIMM totals separate, monitor missing/reset/stale data, save the completed-day same-boot delta search, validate exact counter transitions and reboot behavior, then route UE urgently and CE for owner/vendor-policy review.
visualization: Lead with EDAC-capable expected-host/scope coverage, driver state, poll freshness, counter resets, and missing labels. Plot cumulative CE/UE and derived increases separately by exact scope and boot; show a table with host, scope/physical DIMM map, deltas, totals, sample interval, kernel/driver, BMC/MCE context, maintenance, and owner. Never stack controller totals with their child DIMMs.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable — no CIM data model for DIMM correctable error counters.

knownFalsePositives:
A positive delta is a real counter increase; the false positive is an incorrect operational conclusion or duplicated accounting.

1. **Controller and DIMM hierarchy overlap** — EDAC controller totals aggregate deeper scopes. Display and alert by one chosen granularity; never sum parent and child counts.

2. **Boot/module reload or explicit reset** — counters initialize/reset with driver lifecycle and can decrease. The detector compares only the same boot and nondecreasing sequence; health must record the boundary rather than treating the new total as an error burst.

3. **Stress, burn-in, or vendor memory diagnostics** — approved lab/maintenance tests can generate genuine corrected errors. Match exact host/scope, tool/job, change, owner, bounded interval, and post-test disposition.

4. **Poor DIMM attribution** — some drivers report only controller/row totals or missing labels. A real increase may not identify a physical stick; correlate dmidecode/vendor inventory and BMC/MCE evidence before replacement.

5. **Firmware/kernel/driver mapping change** — upgrades can rename scopes or alter exposure. Reconcile source paths and inventory, and requalify fixtures before comparing history.

6. **Duplicate polling routes** — duplicate samples do not create deltas when identical, but skew timing and trends. Detect and repair duplicate inputs/forwarders.

Suppress notification only for an exact host/scope and test/change with owner, reason, start, and finite expiry. Never suppress UE evidence broadly or hide missing-driver/host/scope, reset, staleness, parse, or source-health findings.
detectionType: same-boot increase in cumulative EDAC memory-error counters
hardware: Linux hosts whose kernel and memory-controller driver expose EDAC sysfs counters. Physical DIMM attribution depends on platform/driver labels and must be reconciled with SMBIOS/BMC/vendor inventory; controller totals can overlap DIMM totals, and hosts without EDAC exposure remain out of coverage.

cost.search_load_notes: Hourly small cumulative-counter samples and an ordered daily delta search; ingest scales with EDAC controllers and exposed DIMM/rank scopes.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and counter semantics

Assign Linux/kernel, hardware/RAS, BMC, workload, Splunk data/content, and incident owners. Inventory supported host, kernel, EDAC driver/module, memory controller, SMBIOS/BMC DIMM locator, physical slot, serial/part, workload, redundancy, maintenance, and vendor escalation. The collector requires read access to exported sysfs counters and `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`; it does not need `reset_counters`, module-load, panic-policy, memory-offline, reboot, or hardware-control rights. This review executed no kernel/platform matrix and asserts no production version compatibility.

Linux documents `ce_count` and `ue_count` as cumulative totals. Correctable errors can be early indications of a failing DIMM and should be reported; uncorrectable counts can remain zero if panic-on-UE stops the host before increment is observed. Controller totals can aggregate child scopes. Therefore compute ordered deltas, never sum successive totals, never add parent and child scopes, and never equate no indexed increment with healthy hardware.

## Step 1 — Collect scope-aware samples

A reviewed host-local script enumerates `/sys/devices/system/edac/mc/mc*`. Emit separate records for each selected controller and supported `(dimm|rank)*` scope with canonical `memory_scope`, exact source path, available DIMM label/location/type/size, numeric CE/UE totals, boot ID, kernel release, EDAC driver/controller name, command status, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Keep a `scope_level` and parent so dashboards prevent double counting. Poll hourly as local policy; use atomic reads as closely together as practical and record partial-read failure.

Maintain expected EDAC-capable hosts/scopes separately. Health reports directory/module absence, no supported driver, missing/changed scope, duplicate path, blank label, nonnumeric/negative/decreasing counter, boot change, stale/future sample, poll/runtime/permission failure, duplicate route, and index delay. A reboot or explicit reset starts a new series; preserve it rather than manufacturing a delta.

## Step 2 — Save and understand the search

Save sidecar SPL as `linux_edac_counter_increase` and run daily over the prior completed day (`earliest=-2d@d latest=-1d@d`) after measured delay. Include enough prior-state summary or overlap in a production implementation to compare the first in-window sample with the last preceding sample; the sidecar intentionally reports only pairs present inside its fixed slice, so document that boundary limitation. A durable summary can store last counter by host/scope/boot after replay/idempotence testing.

The SPL validates identity and nonnegative numeric values, removes exact duplicates, sorts ascending, obtains the immediately previous sample per host/scope, and calculates a delta only when boot IDs match and counters do not decrease. It retains intervals where either delta is positive, sums deltas within that nonoverlapping slice, and routes any UE as critical and CE-only as high local policy. Linux supplies no universal `>10/week` replacement threshold, so none is asserted.

## Step 3 — Validate deltas, resets, and attribution

Replay fixed samples for unchanged, +1/+N CE, +1 UE, simultaneous increase, first sample, same-boot decrease, changed boot, out-of-order/late data, duplicate route, missing/nonnumeric/negative value, controller plus child scope, renamed scope, missing label, and exact dispatch boundaries. Assert no parent/child aggregation and verify source-health records reset/reboot independently.

On an approved nonproduction host, compare sysfs values immediately before and after collection and against `rasdaemon`/journal, machine-check, and BMC/vendor diagnostics where available. Use hardware vendor injection only in a disposable lab under safety guidance; do not force an ECC fault on production. Verify the physical DIMM mapping with vendor UI/SMBIOS and acknowledge when the driver offers controller-only attribution. Keep draft until owners approve scope maps, fixtures, boundary handling, source health, alert routes, dashboard, and response.

## Step 4 — Operationalize with corroboration

Alerts state `EDAC counter increased`, not `DIMM failed`. Include host, scope/label/source path, CE/UE deltas and totals, boot ID, sample interval, kernel/driver, physical mapping confidence, BMC/MCE context, workload/change, source health, and runbook. Responders verify raw counters and boot/reset history; inspect journal/rasdaemon/MCE and BMC logs; map scope to physical component; review firmware, thermals, power, CPU/memory-controller and workload context; run vendor diagnostics in an approved window; and decide observation or replacement under vendor policy. Never change `panic_on_ue`, reset counters, offline pages/DIMMs, reboot, or replace automatically.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot and close

- **No EDAC directory:** verify platform ECC/firmware, kernel config/modules and driver support; record coverage debt rather than fabricating zero.
- **Counts decrease:** inspect boot ID, module reload, reset action, scope replacement/rename, and collector order. Start a new series.
- **Counts appear multiplied:** ensure cumulative values are differenced and parent/controller totals are not added to children.
- **No DIMM label:** preserve controller/row scope, reconcile SMBIOS/BMC/vendor data, and do not guess a slot.
- **UE with no follow-up sample:** the host may have panicked. Correlate availability, crash/MCE, BMC, and forwarding evidence.
- **Late/out-of-order data:** compare event/index time and adjust delayed slices or state summary; never difference ingestion order blindly.

Close only after source health is current, counter/boot/scope evidence is verified, physical attribution confidence and workload impact are documented, vendor diagnosis/remediation or accepted risk is recorded, and an approved observation interval has no unexplained increase.
grandmaExplanation: We compare each new memory-error total with the previous total from the same startup. That shows how many new corrections or serious errors occurred without counting the same old errors again and again.
